title: When Steering Shifts Discourse: Identifying and Intervening on Discourse-Level Changes due to Activation Steering in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.41661v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Activation steering is an inference-time technique used to control or modify the behavior, tone, or safety properties of a large language model (LLM) without retraining the model's weights or editing its input prompt, but simply by adding a vector to its residual-stream activations. However, activation steering also changes the generated text in unintended ways, unrelated to intended behavior change, that are not well understood. Prior work has measured these changes only through coarse signals such as perplexity. In this work, we show that steering systematically produces significant changes in discourse dimensions of the generated text, such as its formality, use of evidence, and ambiguity. We present a way of countering this by adding a second, complementary vector that targets the affected discourse dimension. translated_title: 当引导改变话语：识别与干预大语言模型中激活引导所导致的话语层面变化
translated_abstract: 激活引导是一种推理时技术，用于控制或修改大语言模型（LLM）的行为、语气或安全属性，无需重新训练模型权重或编辑输入提示，只需向模型的残差流激活中添加一个向量即可。然而，激活引导也会以非预期的方式改变生成的文本，这些变化与预期的行为改变无关，且尚未被充分理解。先前的工作仅通过困惑度等粗粒度信号来衡量这些变化。在本工作中，我们表明激活引导会系统性地在生成文本的话语维度上产生显著变化，例如文本的正式程度、证据使用和模糊性。我们提出了一种应对方法，即添加第二个针对受影响话语维度的互补向量。这种干预能够恢复约78%的非预期话语变化，同时保留预期的引导行为。
tldr: 论文揭示了大语言模型的激活引导会系统性改变生成文本的话语层面特征（如正式程度、证据使用和模糊性），并提出通过添加针对受影响维度的互补向量进行干预，可恢复约78%的非预期话语变化，同时保留预期的引导效果。
en_tdlr: The paper reveals that activation steering in LLMs systematically alters discourse-level features of generated text (such as formality, evidence use, and ambiguity), and proposes intervening with a complementary targeting vector that restores about 78% of the unintended discourse changes while preserving the intended steering behavior.
